data.long_meaning: Elzbieta is a Polish name derived from the Hebrew word 'El' meaning 'God' and 'Bieta' meaning 'God's promise'. It was traditionally given to girls born in times of hardship as a reminder of God's covenant. The name Elzbieta carries the meaning “God's Promise” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Elzbieta usually hope their child will grow to embody god's promise and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.meaning: אלזבieta היא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשם אליזבת
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלזבieta הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשם אליזבת, שמקורו בתנ"ך מהשם העברי אלישבע, שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא שבועתי' או 'אלוהים הוא השבועה שלי'. השם אליזבת היה נפוץ בקרב הנוצרים בימי הביניים וניתן לבנות כמתנת אלוהים.

in_greek.name: Ελζβieta
in_greek.long_meaning: Ελζβieta είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος Ελισάβετ, που προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα אלישבע (Elisheva). Το όνομα Ελισάβετ ήταν γνωστό στην Καινή Διαθήκη ως το όνομα της μητέρας του Ιωάννη Βαπτιστού (Λουκ 1:5-45). Η Ελζβieta είναι μια παραλλαγή του ονόματος που χρησιμοποιείται σε πολλές χριστιανικές παραδόσεις.

in_latin.name: Elzbieta
in_latin.long_meaning: Elzbieta est forma christiana nominis Elisabeth, quod derivatur ex hebraeo nomine אלישבע (Elisheva), significans 'Deus est iuramentum meum' vel 'Deus est promissio mea'. Nomen Elisabeth in primitiva ecclesia christiana erat popularis et datum est multis sanctis et viris illustribus.

in_english.name: Elzbieta
in_english.meaning: Elzbieta means 'God is my oath' or 'God's promise'
in_english.long_meaning: Elzbieta is a Christian name derived from the Hebrew name אלישבע (Elisheva), meaning 'God is my oath' or 'God's promise'. The name Elisabeth, from which Elzbieta originates, was popularized in the Christian tradition through the New Testament, particularly as the name of the mother of John the Baptist (Luke 1:5-45). Elzbieta is a variant of the name used in various Christian cultures, symbolizing faith, devotion, and divine promise.

historical_references.reference: Elzbieta Szarlotta, a Polish queen consort, was born on January 12, 1709, in Warsaw, Poland, as the youngest daughter of King Stanisław Leszczyński and Princess Konstancja Ildefonsa of Austria. She married King August III of Poland in 1729, and her influence on him led to the War of the Polish Succession.

Elzbieta Bogumila Chodkiewicz, a noblewoman from the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, was born around 1465 in what is now Belarus. She was a patron of the arts and a patroness of the Jesuits. In 1513, she married Grand Duke Algirdas of Lithuania, and her influence helped to strengthen the position of the Jesuits in the region.
